title: Epic: card payments
description: Four milestones in order; open one for its tasks, a task for how it works

blocks.title: Research
blocks.description: Which provider, which cards, what it costs

children.title: Providers
children.details:
Compared on fees, payout time and EU card coverage.

- **Stripe**: 1.5 % + 25 ct, payout in 2 days
- **Adyen**: interchange++, minimum volume
- **Mollie**: 1.8 % + 25 ct, SEPA included

Chosen: **Stripe**, for the API and the test mode.

children.title: Card types
children.details: Visa and Mastercard cover 96 % of last year's orders. Amex adds 3 % at a higher fee: later.

children.title: Costs
children.details: At 40 000 orders a month and 32 € on average: about 24 000 € a year in fees.

blocks.title: Design
blocks.description: Checkout flow and API contract agreed
blocks.details: Checkout keeps one page. The card form is Stripe Elements, so card numbers never reach our servers. The API contract is `POST /charges` with the order id and an idempotency key.

children.title: Charge service
children.description: One charge per order, retried safely

children.title: Save the charge
children.details:
The idempotency key is the order id, so a retried request never charges twice:

```sql
INSERT INTO charges (order_id, stripe_id, amount)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3)
ON CONFLICT (order_id) DO NOTHING;
```

A conflict means an earlier request already saved this charge: answer with that one.

children.title: Checkout form
children.details: Replaces the card fields of the old form. Errors from Stripe show under the field they belong to.

children.title: Webhooks
children.details: Listens to `charge.refunded` and `charge.dispute.created` and updates the order.

children.title: Load test
children.details: Black Friday peak last year was 140 orders a second. Target: 200, with p95 under 800 ms.

blocks.title: Launch
blocks.details: Week 1: 10 % of customers, compare conversion with the old checkout. Week 2: everyone, if conversion did not drop.
